review.summary: All 57 lexical warnings have explicit source-specific acceptance reasons. The 55 short-proof warnings expose concrete coordinate computations, canonical-map readbacks, or consequences of separately proved operator and colimit laws. The two literal-definition warnings are the exterior degree-zero unit vacuum and zero padding of a six-coordinate embedding with a proved left inverse. This source review complements the compiler and trust audit; it is not itself a kernel proof of mathematical semantics.

Their short simplification proofs evaluate a concrete linear isometry; they do not assume endpoint exchange or replace the Clifford carrier.

The pair-exchange equations are multiplicative consequences of the actual Clifford algebra equivalence and its proved creation/annihilation images. The ordered products are retained in the same noncommutative algebra. The surrounding number-commutator and grade-submodule theorems prove the substantive fixed-number reversal separately.

The two zeros are the required same-mode CAR nilpotency: the mode-4 source or sink is the square of its corresponding null Clifford generator. This does not collapse all pair words: the owner proves sourcePair55 i and sinkPair55 i nonzero when i ≠ 4 and provides the concrete i=0 witness.

The native creation and annihilation elements are real scalar multiples of Clifford generators. The canonical Clifford grade involution negates each generator and preserves real scalar multiplication, yielding these odd-parity equations. They concern Clifford parity, with number grading and local boundary grading stated separately in the owner.

The cone uses the existing GNSStage and GNSHilbertColimit carriers and the canonical stage-to-colimit isometries; the owner separately proves density, transition compatibility, and actual observable intertwining. The rfl statements only expose those already selected maps on the two coordinates.

The vacuum eigenvalue zero is derived from the genuine contraction annihilating the exterior unit, followed by wedge multiplication of zero. The operator is creation composed with contractLeft, not the former constant-zero implementation. Generator evaluation and normalized occupied-state eigenvalue one are proved separately on the same carrier.

It is not used as a substitute for evaluated occupation action: number_op_single_particle_evaluated, number_op_occupied, number_op_square, and number_op_idempotent establish those stronger results from actual contraction laws.

Nonzero claims retain their stated Nontrivial/normalization hypotheses.

The adjacent injectivity, bonding, and universal-lift theorems establish that this is an actual faithful colimit map. The target algebraicCreationElement/algebraicAnnihilationElement are independently owned canonical stage representatives in the tensor colimit. They are not definitions chosen to force the new theorem and are not zero operators; the finite CAR identity has identity as its right-hand side and the colimit map is injective.

Scalars are coefficients of fixed noncommutative CAR matrices, not replacements for the operator carrier. The lemma is used in wittGamma.map_smul, and the independently derived square law validates its Clifford lift.

Its image is the pre-existing matrix difference E 0 0 minus E 1 1, using the mixed-generator calibration. The statement does not conflate this axial charge with global number degree or local endpoint parity; subsequent Hermiticity is derived from adjoint CAR occupation matrices.

The rfl theorem exposes an actual algebra-homomorphism composition: calibrated real Clifford matrices followed by the existing entrywise real-to-complex map and coherent matrix reindexing. Its target remains the full coherent complex matrix stage. The existing star-readback law and derived creation-adjoint relation support the later Hermitian Hamiltonian specialization; no star operation on native Cl55 is presumed.

The short simp proof is the universal Clifford-lift generator computation rule. The lift is constructed from the concrete linear wittGamma map and its proved Q55 square relation, which was derived from the native matrix CAR laws. It does not assume the generator calibration as a target-valued structure field; the creation and annihilation readbacks are subsequently derived with their required one-half normalization.

Raw native number and raw matrix occupation are independently defined as sums of the corresponding creation-annihilation products. Their equality is obtained by the proved generator calibration and algebra-map sum/product laws. Centering then uses the separately proved exact 5/2 identity correction. The associated commutator theorem removes only this central scalar term, preserving the actual native number grading rather than transporting an arbitrary grader by definition.

The two rfl lemmas correctly expose the forward function and algebra-homomorphism projection of AlgEquiv.ofBijective applied to the same calibrated universal Clifford representation. Bijectivity is proved separately: source simplicity gives injectivity, and the established finite-dimensional spinor/stage dimension equality gives surjectivity. Thus these projections retain the named-generator calibration; they do not substitute an arbitrary carrier equivalence for the representation.

Its value is the determinant of the two lower spinors, and the established twistorPairPlucker construction has precisely that expression as its p23 minor. The companion equality with the pulled-back alternating determinant and the proved radical identify the intended form. Short rfl proofs are appropriate coordinate interface lemmas here.

The proofs establish alternation and skew symmetry of the explicit lower-spinor determinant by commutative ring algebra. Vanishing on (Z,Z) is the defining alternating behavior, not evidence that the form is identically zero: its displayed formula evaluates to one on lower spinors (1,0) and (0,1). Neither theorem has a hypothesis supplying the requested conclusion.

The translation is the actual linear equivalence (omega,pi) mapped to (omega + i*A*pi,pi), with the inverse and linearity proved in its construction. It leaves the lower spinor unchanged, so preservation of its determinant pairing is definitional. The separate translation_incidence theorem shows that this same map sends the native X incidence plane to the X+A plane; the preserved pairing has not been obtained by defining translation to be the identity.

The p23 readout records the p01/p23 exchange in the explicit exterior-square block-swap map; blockSwapPlucker_pluckerLine proves that it is induced by swapping the actual four-vector blocks. The polar readout evaluates the owned Klein polar form against infinityPlucker, which is the wedge of the first two coordinate vectors and has coordinates (1,0,0,0,0,0). This gives p23 and identifies the infinity covector with the polar dual of that plane. Both short proofs express concrete coordinate laws, and the form and block transformation remain distinct objects.

The reported text conformalSixToPAC55 := 0 is a lexical misidentification of a structure-valued definition. Only the four unused target coordinates x1,x2,x3,y3 are zero. The map retains all six independent inputs as x0=a0, y0=ax, y1=ay, y2=az, u=bz, v=b0. The explicit native readback composed with conformalSixToV55 is proved equal to the original input, yielding injectivity; native Clifford generator injectivity is also proved. The quadratic form restricts to quadratic24. This is a six-to-ten coordinate embedding with zero padding, not a constant map or a scalar proxy.

The normalized interval is defined from the owned Klein polar form divided by the two p23 chart coordinates. graphPlucker is the actual wedge of the two graph-frame columns, not a determinant-valued replacement. Its p23 coordinate is proved to be one and its polar pairing is independently computed as det(X-Y). The short simp proof combines those facts to evaluate the normalization; the nonzero chart denominators are supplied by the graph construction itself.

For arbitrary X,Y and lower spinors pi,rho, graphIncidence has lower component exactly pi or rho. The infinity form is the determinant of those lower components, so it agrees with evaluation on (0,pi),(0,rho). The right-hand side is a potentially nonzero spinor determinant, not a manufactured constant. This helper supports the actual frame-scaling and infinity-normalized interval theorems, whose nondegenerate-frame hypotheses remain explicit.

The convention adapter is a genuine complex linear equivalence: it multiplies the upper spinor by -i and its inverse multiplies by i, leaving the lower spinor fixed. graphIncidence is explicitly its composition with the pre-existing native incidenceLinearMap, so the i factors cancel to give (X*pi,pi). Conversely the raw native incidence is graph incidence at i*X. These are justified convention/readout lemmas; the same owner connects the frame to the existing twistorPairPlucker and proves the native incidence-plane intersection criterion. No real signature or modular identification is inferred from these short identities.

The map is constructed as a linear equivalence with these inverse laws; the short involutivity proof checks its concrete scalar action. Its exterior-square compatibility is proved separately, so these helpers are not an assumed reflection law or an identity-map substitute.

The same concrete map is proved to intertwine lorentzPlucker with the signed Plucker action and the six-coordinate embedding with the native global sheet reflection, then with the Clifford action.
